questions.question: What is the primary definition of 'Scalability' in a software system?

options.A: The ability to make the source code shorter.
options.B: The measure of a system’s ability to handle growing amounts of work by adding resources.
options.C: The speed at which a single user can navigate the site.
options.D: The physical size of the server hardware.

questions.question: True or False: 'Vertical Scaling' (Scaling Up) involves adding more power (CPU, RAM) to an existing server.

options.B: False

questions.question: Which of the following are benefits of 'Horizontal Scaling' (Scaling Out)? (Select all that apply)

options.A: Easier to achieve high availability and redundancy.
options.B: No theoretical limit to how much you can scale.
options.C: Generally more cost-effective using commodity hardware.
options.D: Decreases the number of servers you have to manage.

questions.question: What does 'Elasticity' refer to in cloud computing?

options.A: The ability of a system to grow and shrink resources automatically based on demand.
options.B: The physical flexibility of network cables.
options.C: The ability to use different programming languages.
options.D: A system that never crashes.

questions.question: True or False: Horizontal scaling usually requires a Load Balancer to distribute traffic among multiple servers.

options.B: False

questions.question: Which of these are common 'Bottlenecks' that prevent a system from scaling? (Select all that apply)

options.B: Network bandwidth.
options.C: Poorly optimized code/algorithms.
options.D: The color of the website's logo.

questions.question: What is 'Latency' in the context of system performance?

options.A: The total number of users on the site.
options.B: The time it takes for a request to travel from the sender to the receiver and back.
options.C: The amount of data stored in the database.
options.D: The number of lines of code written per day.

questions.question: True or False: Vertical scaling is limited by the maximum capacity of a single machine.

options.B: False

questions.question: Which of the following are 'Stateless' components (easier to scale)? (Select all that apply)

options.A: Web servers that don't store session data locally.
options.B: Image processing microservices.
options.C: A primary SQL database.
options.D: A local file system used for temporary storage.

questions.question: What is the primary role of a 'Load Balancer'?

options.A: To encrypt all data on the server.
options.B: To distribute incoming network traffic across a group of backend servers.
options.C: To write code automatically.
options.D: To monitor the temperature of the data center.

questions.question: True or False: Adding more servers always results in a linear increase in performance (e.g., 2x servers = 2x speed).

options.B: False (Overhead of communication usually prevents perfect linearity)

questions.question: Which of these are strategies to improve 'Database Scalability'? (Select all that apply)

options.B: Sharding (Partitioning).
options.C: Caching.
options.D: Deleting old data.

questions.question: What is a 'Single Point of Failure' (SPOF)?

options.A: A bug in a single line of code.
options.B: A part of a system that, if it fails, will stop the entire system from working.
options.C: A user who logs in only once.
options.D: A server that has only one CPU.

questions.question: True or False: Caching can improve scalability by reducing the load on the primary database.

options.B: False

questions.question: What are the common layers where 'Caching' can be implemented? (Select all that apply)

options.B: Content Delivery Network (CDN).
options.C: Database-level (e.g., Redis/Memcached).
options.D: Physical CPU cache.

questions.question: What does 'Throughput' measure?

options.A: The time it takes to process a single request.
options.B: The number of requests a system can handle in a given time period (e.g., Requests Per Second).
options.C: The weight of the server racks.
options.D: The number of developers working on the project.

questions.question: True or False: A system that is 'Highly Available' is always 100% scalable.

options.B: False

questions.question: Which of the following is a key characteristic of a 'Microservices' architecture regarding scalability?

options.A: It requires all services to be on the same server.
options.B: It allows individual features to be scaled independently based on their specific demand.
options.C: It eliminates the need for a database.
options.D: It makes the code harder to read.

questions.question: Which 'Load Balancing' algorithms are commonly used? (Select all that apply)

options.B: Least Connections.
options.C: IP Hash.
options.D: Random Walk.

questions.question: True or False: Scaling out is generally more complex to implement than scaling up.

options.B: False

questions.question: What is 'Read/Write Splitting'?

options.A: Dividing the code into two files.
options.B: Directing all 'read' queries to replica databases and all 'write' queries to a primary database.
options.C: Using two different keyboards for coding.
options.D: Sorting data by alphabetical order.

questions.question: Which factors contribute to 'High Availability' (HA)? (Select all that apply)

options.B: Failover mechanisms.
options.C: Geographic distribution.
options.D: Using a dark mode theme.

questions.question: True or False: A CDN (Content Delivery Network) helps scale by serving static content from servers closer to the user.

options.B: False

questions.question: What is 'Asynchronous Processing'?

options.A: Processing everything at the exact same time.
options.B: Offloading time-consuming tasks to a background worker so the main application can remain responsive.
options.C: Deleting tasks that take too long.
options.D: A way to encrypt data.

questions.question: Which of these are valid 'Vertical Scaling' upgrades? (Select all that apply)

options.B: Moving from a 4-core to a 32-core CPU.
options.C: Adding 10 more identical servers.
options.D: Switching from HDD to NVMe SSD.

questions.question: True or False: Stateless applications are easier to scale horizontally than stateful applications.

options.B: False

questions.question: What is 'Database Sharding'?

options.A: Backing up the database every hour.
options.B: Horizontal partitioning of data across multiple database instances.
options.C: Converting SQL to NoSQL.
options.D: Deleting old user accounts.

questions.question: Which metrics are used to measure 'Reliability'? (Select all that apply)

options.B: Uptime percentage (e.g., 99.9%).
options.C: Error rates.
options.D: Total lines of documentation.

questions.question: True or False: In a 'Shared-Nothing' architecture, each node is independent and self-sufficient.

options.B: False

questions.question: What does the '99th Percentile' (P99) latency represent?

options.A: The average latency of all users.
options.B: The maximum latency experienced by the slowest 1% of users.
options.C: The speed of the server's CPU.
options.D: The percentage of users who liked the site.

questions.question: Which of these can help handle sudden 'Traffic Spikes'? (Select all that apply)

options.B: Queueing systems.
options.C: Rate limiting.
options.D: Manual server restarts.

questions.question: True or False: Over-provisioning (keeping extra resources 'just in case') is the most cost-effective way to scale.

options.B: False

questions.question: What is 'Failover'?

options.A: When a system crashes and stays down.
options.B: The automatic switching to a redundant or standby computer server, system, or network upon the failure of the previously active one.
options.C: A way to uninstall software.
options.D: The process of moving code to production.

questions.question: In the context of scaling, what is the 'Master-Slave' (Primary-Secondary) database pattern primarily used for?

options.B: To distribute read traffic across multiple replicas while keeping writes on a single node.
options.C: To delete old data automatically.
options.D: To make the database look more organized.

questions.question: True or False: 'Scalability' and 'Performance' are the same thing; if a system is fast, it is also scalable.

options.B: False

questions.question: Which of the following are characteristics of 'Cloud Elasticity'? (Select all that apply)

options.B: Pay-as-you-go pricing based on actual resource usage.
options.C: Requires manual hardware installation for every spike.
options.D: Enables cost optimization during low-traffic periods.

questions.question: What is 'Stateful' vs 'Stateless' scaling?

options.A: Stateful apps are easier to scale because they remember the user.
options.B: Stateless apps are easier to scale because any server can handle any request without local session data.
options.C: They are the same thing in modern cloud environments.
options.D: Stateful scaling only works for CSS files.

questions.question: True or False: A 'Single Point of Failure' (SPOF) can be eliminated by adding redundancy to critical components.

options.B: False

questions.question: Which of these are valid methods for 'Session Management' in a scalable web cluster? (Select all that apply)

options.B: Distributed Cache (e.g., Redis).
options.C: Client-side storage (e.g., JWT tokens).
options.D: Storing sessions in a local text file on each server.

questions.question: What does 'SLA' stand for in system operations?

options.B: Service Level Agreement.
options.C: Standard Loading Action.
options.D: Simple Log Analysis.

questions.question: True or False: Horizontal scaling is generally more difficult for relational databases (SQL) than for web servers.

options.B: False

questions.question: Which of these are 'Frontend' scaling techniques? (Select all that apply)

options.B: Using a Content Delivery Network (CDN).
options.C: Compressing images.
options.D: Changing the font size.

questions.question: What is 'Response Time'?

options.A: The time it takes to write the code.
options.B: The total time from when a user sends a request until they receive a response.
options.C: The speed of the user's typing.
options.D: The time the server is turned off.

questions.question: True or False: Vertical scaling (Scaling Up) usually requires downtime to upgrade hardware (RAM/CPU).

options.B: False

questions.question: Which of the following metrics are key to monitoring 'Scalability'? (Select all that apply)

options.B: Memory Usage.
options.C: Requests Per Second (RPS).
options.D: Number of coffee cups on the developer's desk.

questions.question: What is 'Geographic Redundancy'?

options.A: Having two servers in the same room.
options.B: Deploying the same system in different physical locations (regions) to protect against local disasters.
options.C: Translating the app into different languages.
options.D: Naming servers after different cities.

questions.question: True or False: NoSQL databases (like MongoDB) are often designed to scale out (horizontally) more easily than traditional SQL databases.

options.B: False

questions.question: Which of these are 'Caching' eviction policies? (Select all that apply)

options.B: FIFO (First In First Out).
options.C: LFU (Least Frequently Used).
options.D: ABC (Alphabetical Order).

questions.question: What is 'Cold Start' latency in the context of serverless scaling?

options.A: The time it takes to start the server in a cold room.
options.B: The delay that occurs when a serverless function is triggered for the first time after being idle.
options.C: The time it takes to boot a computer in winter.
options.D: A type of database error.

questions.question: True or False: 'Auto-scaling' allows you to add servers automatically when CPU usage exceeds a certain threshold.

options.B: False

questions.question: Which of the following describes 'Availability' (The 'A' in High Availability)?

options.B: The percentage of time the system is operational and accessible to users.
options.C: The number of features available in the app.
options.D: The size of the hard drive.

questions.question: Which of these are benefits of 'Asynchronous Workflows'? (Select all that apply)

options.A: Reduced blocking on the main application thread.
options.B: Better handling of bursty traffic.
options.C: Ability to retry failed background tasks without user impact.
options.D: Makes every request 100% instantaneous.

questions.question: True or False: Using a 'Microservices' architecture eliminates the need for load balancers.

options.B: False

questions.question: What is a 'Global Load Balancer' (GSLB)?

options.A: A load balancer that works for the whole world.
options.B: A system that routes traffic to different data centers based on the user's location or server health.
options.C: A very large physical machine.
options.D: A way to balance the weight of global servers.

questions.question: Which of these contribute to 'Database Bottlenecks'? (Select all that apply)

options.A: Missing indexes on frequently searched columns.
options.B: Too many concurrent connections.
options.C: Extremely large table sizes without partitioning.
options.D: Using a pretty font for the database console.

questions.question: True or False: 'Scalability' can be achieved by writing more efficient code (Optimization).

options.A: True (It's the first step before adding hardware)
options.B: False

questions.question: What is 'Service Discovery' in a scalable architecture?

options.A: Finding new services to buy online.
options.B: The automatic detection of network locations for service instances.
options.C: Writing a list of services in a Word document.
options.D: Naming the microservices correctly.

questions.question: Which 'Cloud' features assist in building scalable systems? (Select all that apply)

options.B: Object Storage (e.g., S3).
options.C: Serverless Functions (e.g., Lambda).
options.D: Physical hard drive shredding.

questions.question: True or False: All bottlenecks in a system are related to hardware.

options.B: False (Software configuration and algorithms are often bottlenecks)

questions.question: What is 'Throttling' (Rate Limiting)?

options.B: Purposely limiting the number of requests a user or client can make in a specific timeframe.
options.C: A type of database compression.
options.D: Deleting slow users.

questions.question: Which of the following can cause 'Network Latency'? (Select all that apply)

options.A: Physical distance between client and server.
options.B: Large numbers of network 'hops'.
options.C: High network congestion.
options.D: The color of the ethernet cables.

questions.question: True or False: Horizontal scaling usually makes the system more resilient to hardware failure.

options.B: False

questions.question: What is 'Over-provisioning'?

options.B: Allocating more resources than are currently needed to ensure capacity for spikes.
options.C: Using only one server.
options.D: Buying too much coffee for the office.

questions.question: Which of these are valid 'Scale-Out' architectures? (Select all that apply)

options.B: Client-Server with multiple backends.
options.C: Cluster computing.
options.D: A single mainframe computer.

questions.question: True or False: 'Failover' should ideally be transparent to the end user.

options.B: False

questions.question: What is a 'Stateless' service?

options.A: A service that has no country.
options.B: A service that does not store any data about previous requests locally.
options.C: A service that is always turned off.
options.D: A service with no code.

questions.question: Which of the following describes the 'C' in the CAP Theorem as it relates to distributed systems?

options.A: Every request receives a response about whether it succeeded or failed.
options.B: Every read receives the most recent write or an error.
options.C: The system continues to operate despite an arbitrary number of messages being dropped.
options.D: The system can handle a high number of concurrent users.

questions.question: What is the primary problem solved by 'Consistent Hashing' in a distributed caching system?

options.B: It minimizes the number of keys that need to be remapped when a cache node is added or removed.
options.C: It ensures that all cache nodes have the exact same data.
options.D: It speeds up the database write operations.

questions.question: True or False: According to the CAP Theorem, a distributed system can simultaneously provide more than two out of the three guarantees (Consistency, Availability, Partition Tolerance).

options.B: False

questions.question: Which of these are valid 'Database Sharding' strategies? (Select all that apply)

options.B: Range-based sharding.
options.C: Directory-based sharding.
options.D: Vertical sharding (splitting by column).

questions.question: What is 'Write Amplification' in the context of distributed databases?

options.A: Writing data to multiple replicas to ensure safety.
options.B: The phenomenon where the amount of data physically written to storage is a multiple of the data logically written by the application.
options.C: Increasing the volume of the server's alarm.
options.D: A way to speed up SQL queries.

questions.question: True or False: 'Quorum-based' writes ensure that a write is considered successful only after a majority of replicas acknowledge it.

options.B: False

questions.question: Which of these are challenges associated with 'Database Sharding'? (Select all that apply)

options.B: Difficulty in maintaining referential integrity (Foreign Keys).
options.C: Rebalancing data when a shard becomes too large.
options.D: Making the database schema too simple.

questions.question: What is the 'Split-Brain' scenario in a distributed cluster?

options.A: When a developer forgets how the system works.
options.B: When a network partition causes a cluster to divide into two independent groups, both believing they are the leader.
options.C: A type of CPU failure.
options.D: When the database is split into two tables.

questions.question: True or False: 'Eventual Consistency' guarantees that if no new updates are made to a data item, eventually all accesses will return the last updated value.

options.B: False

questions.question: Which of the following are 'Distributed Consensus' algorithms? (Select all that apply)

options.B: Raft.
options.C: Zab (Zookeeper Atomic Broadcast).
options.D: QuickSort.

questions.question: In the context of scaling, what does 'Amhdahl's Law' describe?

options.A: The theoretical speedup in latency of the execution of a task at a fixed workload that can be expected of a system whose resources are improved.
options.B: The number of transistors on a chip doubles every two years.
options.C: The price of servers decreases over time.
options.D: The speed of light limits network latency.

questions.question: True or False: 'Strong Consistency' is easier to scale horizontally than 'Eventual Consistency'.

options.B: False

questions.question: Which of these are techniques for 'Cache Warming'? (Select all that apply)

options.A: Pre-populating the cache with frequently accessed data during startup.
options.B: Using a script to simulate user traffic after a deployment.
options.C: Leaving the servers on a high temperature.
options.D: Replaying production logs to fill the cache.

questions.question: What is a 'Hot Partition' (or Hot Key) in a distributed system?

options.A: A server that is physically overheating.
options.B: A single shard or key that receives a disproportionately high amount of traffic, leading to a bottleneck.
options.C: A partition that contains deleted data.
options.D: A way to speed up the database.

questions.question: True or False: 'Load Shedding' is the practice of intentionally dropping low-priority requests to keep the system stable during extreme overload.

options.B: False

questions.question: Which of these are valid 'Global Secondary Index' (GSI) strategies? (Select all that apply)

options.B: Synchronous index updates.
options.C: Local secondary indexes on every shard.
options.D: Storing the index in a physical book.

questions.question: What is 'Backpressure' in a distributed pipeline?

options.A: Pressure from the manager to finish the project.
options.B: The resistance or force opposed to the flow of data in a software system, signaling a downstream component is overwhelmed.
options.C: Air pressure inside the server chassis.
options.D: A type of network error.

questions.question: True or False: 'Sticky Sessions' can cause load imbalance if a few sessions are much more 'heavy' than others.

options.B: False

questions.question: What is 'Gossip Protocol' used for in a distributed cluster?

options.A: For developers to talk about their coworkers.
options.B: For nodes to periodically share state and membership information with a few random neighbors to ensure eventual cluster-wide awareness.
options.C: To broadcast errors to the user.
options.D: To encrypt the network traffic.

questions.question: Which of these describe the 'Saga Pattern' for distributed transactions? (Select all that apply)

options.B: Compensating transactions to undo changes if a step fails.
options.C: Using a single global lock on the whole database.
options.D: Coordinating via an orchestrator or events.

questions.question: True or False: 'Active-Active' multi-region deployments are generally simpler to manage than 'Active-Passive'.

options.B: False

questions.question: What is the 'Cache Aside' pattern?

options.A: Putting the cache server in a different room.
options.B: The application first checks the cache; if not found, it hits the database and then updates the cache.
options.C: The database automatically updates the cache.
options.D: Deleting the cache every hour.

questions.question: Which of the following can cause 'Cascading Failures'? (Select all that apply)

options.A: Improperly configured retry logic without exponential backoff.
options.B: A single service failure increasing the load on remaining healthy services.
options.C: Lack of circuit breakers.
options.D: Using a consistent naming convention.

questions.question: True or False: In a 'Write-Through' cache, data is written into the cache and the corresponding database at the same time.

options.B: False

questions.question: What is 'Database Federation'?

options.A: A group of databases forming a government.
options.B: Splitting a single monolithic database into several separate databases based on functional areas (e.g., User DB, Order DB).
options.C: Merging all databases into one.
options.D: A type of database backup.

questions.question: Which of these are valid 'Caching' consistency challenges? (Select all that apply)

options.B: Thundering Herd (Many requests hit the DB at once on cache miss).
options.C: Cache Penetration (Requests for non-existent keys hit the DB).
options.D: Cache servers running out of disk space.

questions.question: True or False: 'Consistent Hashing' requires a centralized server to keep track of which node holds which key.

options.B: False (It uses a hash ring logic that nodes can compute independently)

questions.question: What is 'Optimistic Concurrency Control' (OCC)?

options.A: Hoping that no two users update the same record.
options.B: Allowing multiple transactions to proceed without locks, then checking for conflicts before committing.
options.C: Using a lock for every single read operation.
options.D: A way to speed up the network.

questions.question: Which of the following are true about 'Vector Clocks'? (Select all that apply)

options.A: They are used to determine the partial ordering of events in a distributed system.
options.B: They help detect causality violations and conflicts.
options.C: They are used to sync the actual time of day on all servers.
options.D: They grow in size as the number of nodes in the cluster increases.

questions.question: True or False: 'Two-Phase Commit' (2PC) is a blocking protocol that can lead to performance bottlenecks in high-scale systems.

options.B: False

questions.question: What is 'Jitter' in the context of network latency or retries?

options.A: The physical shaking of the server.
options.B: Random variation in timing to prevent synchronized requests from overwhelming a system.
options.C: The speed of the mouse cursor.
options.D: A type of network noise.

questions.question: Which of these are valid 'High Availability' deployment models? (Select all that apply)

options.B: Active-Active with Load Balancing.
options.C: N+1 Redundancy.
options.D: Single Instance with RAID 1.

questions.question: True or False: 'Write-Back' (Write-Behind) caching improves write performance by writing to the cache first and asynchronously updating the database later.

options.B: False

questions.question: What is 'Service Mesh' (e.g., Istio, Linkerd)?

options.A: A type of physical network cable.
options.B: A dedicated infrastructure layer for handling service-to-service communication, providing security, observability, and traffic management.
options.C: A tool for designing websites.
options.D: A way to compress the source code.

questions.question: Which of the following are 'Distributed Tracing' concepts? (Select all that apply)

options.B: Span.
options.C: Parent/Child relationship.
options.D: Database index.

questions.question: True or False: 'Connection Pooling' reduces the overhead of establishing a new database connection for every request.

options.B: False

questions.question: What is 'Stateless' vs 'Stateful' in a Load Balancer?

options.A: Stateless load balancers are physically smaller.
options.B: Stateful load balancers maintain information about existing connections; stateless ones treat every packet independently.
options.C: They are the same thing.
options.D: Stateful load balancers are only for SQL.

questions.question: Which of these are valid 'Data Locality' strategies? (Select all that apply)

options.A: Caching data near the compute resources.
options.B: Storing data in the same region as the user.
options.C: Moving code to where the data is (Edge computing).
options.D: Deleting data to save space.

questions.question: True or False: 'Linearizability' is the strongest consistency model, where every operation appears to take place atomically at some point between its invocation and completion.

options.B: False

questions.question: What is 'Head-of-Line Blocking' in a network context?

options.A: When the boss blocks a project.
options.B: When a single slow request blocks subsequent requests in a queue or on a shared connection.
options.C: A type of physical network jam.
options.D: A way to speed up the internet.

questions.question: Which of the following describe 'Bloom Filters'? (Select all that apply)

options.B: Used to test whether an element is a member of a set.
options.C: It can have false positives but no false negatives.
options.D: It can be used to store actual values of the items.

questions.question: True or False: 'Server-Side Rendering' (SSR) is generally easier to scale than 'Client-Side Rendering' (CSR) because the server does less work per request.

options.B: False (The server does more work in SSR)

questions.question: What is 'Distributed Locking'?

options.A: Locking the office door from home.
options.B: A mechanism to ensure that only one process in a distributed system can access a shared resource at a time (e.g., using Redis or Zookeeper).
options.C: Putting a password on every file.
options.D: A way to encrypt the database.

questions.question: Which of these describe 'Blue-Green' deployment? (Select all that apply)

options.B: One environment (Blue) is live, the other (Green) is idle/testing.
options.C: Instant cutover via a load balancer.
options.D: Gradually rolling out to 10% of users.

questions.question: True or False: 'Quorum' in a distributed system (N replicas) is typically defined as W + R > N (where W is write quorum and R is read quorum).

options.B: False

questions.question: What is 'Tail Latency'?

options.A: The speed of the network cable.
options.B: The high-percentile latency (e.g., P99, P99.9) experienced by a small fraction of users.
options.C: The latency at the end of the day.
options.D: A type of database error.

questions.question: Which of these are 'Database Consistency' levels in NoSQL? (Select all that apply)

options.B: Eventual.
options.C: Bounded Staleness.
options.D: High.

questions.question: True or False: 'Rate Limiting' at the API Gateway level can prevent 'Brute Force' attacks.

options.B: False

questions.question: What is 'Database Denormalization'?

options.A: Following the standard rules of database design.
options.B: Purposefully adding redundant data to a database to improve read performance by avoiding complex joins.
options.C: Deleting all indexes.
options.D: A way to encrypt the data.

questions.question: Which of the following are valid 'Scalability' trade-offs? (Select all that apply)

options.B: Cost vs. Performance.
options.C: Consistency vs. Availability.
options.D: Dark Mode vs. Light Mode.

questions.question: True or False: 'Horizontal Partitioning' and 'Sharding' refer to the same basic concept of splitting data across nodes.

options.B: False

questions.question: What is 'Pre-computation' in a scalable system?

options.A: Doing the math before the meeting.
options.B: Calculating and storing results (e.g., reports, aggregates) in advance so they can be retrieved instantly.
options.C: A way to speed up the CPU.
options.D: Deleting unused data.

questions.question: Which of these are 'Health Check' methods? (Select all that apply)

options.B: Readiness Probe.
options.C: Startup Probe.
options.D: Physical Pulse Check.

questions.question: True or False: 'CDN' is only useful for images and videos, not for JSON data.

options.B: False (Dynamic content can also be cached/accelerated)

questions.question: What is 'Exponential Backoff'?

options.B: A retry strategy that increases the wait time between retries exponentially to avoid overwhelming a failing system.
options.C: A type of mathematical formula.
options.D: A way to shut down a server.

questions.question: Which of the following are true about 'Micro-frontends'? (Select all that apply)

options.A: They allow for independent scaling of different parts of the UI.
options.B: They enable independent team deployments.
options.C: They eliminate the need for CSS.
options.D: They can lead to duplicated dependencies if not managed.

questions.question: True or False: 'Sticky Load Balancing' is required for all stateful applications.

options.A: True (Unless using a distributed session store)
options.B: False

questions.question: What is 'Fan-out' in a messaging architecture?

options.A: Using a fan to cool the servers.
options.B: Sending a single message to multiple queues or subscribers simultaneously.
options.C: The process of many users logging out.
options.D: A type of network error.

questions.question: Which of the following are valid 'Scalability' patterns? (Select all that apply)

options.B: Event Sourcing.
options.C: Database Mirroring.
options.D: Manual Data Entry.

questions.question: True or False: 'Caching' at the database level is always faster than 'Caching' at the application level.

options.B: False (App-level cache avoids network round-trip to DB)

questions.question: What is 'Graceful Degradation'?

options.A: When a server falls down politely.
options.B: The ability of a system to maintain at least partial functionality when some portions are inoperative.
options.C: A type of code cleanup.
options.D: A way to uninstall software.

questions.question: What is the primary difference between Vertical and Horizontal scaling?

options.A: Vertical adds more machines; Horizontal adds more RAM to one machine.
options.B: Vertical increases the capacity of a single node; Horizontal adds more nodes to the system.
options.C: Horizontal is for databases; Vertical is for web servers.
options.D: There is no difference in modern cloud environments.

questions.question: True or False: 'Availability' is a measure of the percentage of time a system remains operational and accessible to users.

options.B: False

questions.question: Which of the following are benefits of Horizontal Scaling? (Select all that apply)

options.A: Provides better redundancy and fault tolerance.
options.B: Allows for virtually infinite scaling by adding more commodity hardware.
options.C: Reduces the complexity of application state management.
options.D: Enables zero-downtime upgrades by using rolling deployments.

questions.question: In the context of scalability, what does 'Latency' represent?

options.A: The number of requests a system can handle per second.
options.B: The time delay between a user request and the system's response.
options.C: The physical size of the data stored in the database.
options.D: The amount of power consumed by the server rack.

questions.question: True or False: A 'Single Point of Failure' (SPOF) is a component that, if it fails, stops the entire system from functioning.

options.B: False

questions.question: Which of these are common 'Caching' layers in a web architecture? (Select all that apply)

options.B: In-memory database (e.g., Redis).
options.C: Browser/Client-side cache.
options.D: Physical CPU L1/L2 cache.

questions.question: What is 'Elasticity' in cloud computing?

options.A: The ability to stretch network cables over long distances.
options.B: The ability of a system to automatically scale resources up or down based on real-time demand.
options.C: The flexibility of the database schema.
options.D: A system that can recover from a physical crash.

questions.question: True or False: Vertical scaling (Scaling Up) usually requires no downtime for hardware changes.

options.B: False (It often requires a restart or migration to a larger instance)

questions.question: Which factors typically contribute to 'Database Bottlenecks'? (Select all that apply)

options.A: Lack of proper indexing on high-traffic tables.
options.B: Extremely high numbers of concurrent read/write operations.
options.C: Using a normalized schema.
options.D: Slow disk I/O performance.

questions.question: What is the primary function of a 'Load Balancer'?

options.A: To compress images for faster delivery.
options.B: To distribute incoming network traffic across a group of backend servers.
options.C: To encrypt the primary database.
options.D: To monitor the temperature of the data center.

questions.question: True or False: 'Stateless' applications are generally harder to scale horizontally than 'Stateful' applications.

options.B: False

questions.question: Which 'Load Balancing' algorithms are considered industry standards? (Select all that apply)

options.B: Least Connections.
options.C: IP Hashing.
options.D: Alphabetical Sequencing.

questions.question: What is 'Database Sharding'?

options.A: Cleaning up deleted records to save space.
options.B: Horizontal partitioning of data across multiple independent database instances.
options.C: Merging several small databases into one large one.
options.D: Encrypting the database for security.

questions.question: True or False: A Content Delivery Network (CDN) helps scale by serving static content from edge locations closer to the user.

options.B: False

questions.question: What does 'Throughput' measure in a system?

options.A: The time it takes to process a single request.
options.B: The number of units of information a system can process in a given amount of time.
options.C: The percentage of users who stayed on the site.
options.D: The number of lines of code in the project.

questions.question: True or False: 'Failover' is the process of switching to a redundant or standby server when the primary server fails.

options.B: False

questions.question: Which of these are common strategies for 'Session Management' in a scalable system? (Select all that apply)

options.B: Centralized Session Store (e.g., Redis).
options.C: Client-side Session (e.g., Signed Cookies/JWT).
options.D: Local file-based storage on each web node.

questions.question: What is 'Read/Write Splitting' in a database cluster?

options.A: Deleting half of the database to make it faster.
options.B: Directing all read queries to replicas while keeping all write operations on a primary node.
options.C: Using different languages for reading and writing data.
options.D: Splitting the database by alphabetical order.

questions.question: True or False: Horizontal scaling usually makes a system more resilient to hardware failures compared to vertical scaling.

options.B: False

questions.question: Which metrics are essential for monitoring a system's 'Scalability' health? (Select all that apply)

options.B: Network I/O Wait times.
options.C: Request Error Rates (5xx).
options.D: Total number of Git commits.

questions.question: What is 'Asynchronous Processing'?

options.A: Processing everything in the order it was received without delay.
options.B: Offloading tasks to a background queue to allow the main application thread to remain responsive.
options.C: Stopping all requests until the database finishes an update.
options.D: A type of database compression.

questions.question: True or False: 'Auto-scaling' is a cloud-native feature that adds or removes server instances automatically based on defined metrics.

options.B: False

questions.question: What is the primary benefit of using a CDN (Content Delivery Network)?

options.A: It secures the backend database with encryption.
options.B: It reduces latency by serving static assets from edge servers located closer to the user.
options.C: It replaces the need for an application server.
options.D: It automatically generates CSS for the frontend.

questions.question: True or False: In a 'Stateless' architecture, any server in a cluster can handle any incoming request because no session data is stored locally on the server.

options.B: False

questions.question: Which of the following help mitigate a 'Single Point of Failure' (SPOF)? (Select all that apply)

options.B: Using automated failover mechanisms.
options.C: Deploying across multiple geographic regions.
options.D: Consolidating all services onto one high-powered server.

questions.question: Which term describes a system's ability to automatically grow and shrink resources based on current demand?

options.B: Elasticity
options.C: Persistence
options.D: Normalization

questions.question: True or False: Vertical scaling (Scaling Up) is usually more cost-effective than horizontal scaling for very large-scale systems.

options.B: False

questions.question: What are common triggers for an 'Auto-scaling' event? (Select all that apply)

options.B: Increased number of active network connections.
options.C: Low memory availability.
options.D: The number of lines of code in a pull request.

questions.question: According to the CAP Theorem, when a network partition occurs (P), what must a distributed system choose between?

options.B: Consistency (C) and Availability (A)
options.C: Security and Performance
options.D: Storage and Memory

questions.question: True or False: 'Eventual Consistency' guarantees that if no new updates are made to a data item, eventually all accesses will return the last updated value.

options.B: False

questions.question: Which of the following are valid 'Database Sharding' strategies? (Select all that apply)

options.B: Range-based Sharding.
options.C: Directory-based Sharding.
options.D: Vertical Sharding (moving columns to different tables).

questions.question: What is the 'Thundering Herd' problem in a caching system?

options.A: A physical failure of the cache hardware.
options.B: Many concurrent requests hitting the database simultaneously when a popular cache key expires.
options.C: When the cache stores too much data for the RAM.
options.D: A security vulnerability involving duplicate keys.

questions.question: True or False: 'Sticky Sessions' (Session Affinity) are required if an application stores user session data in the local memory of a specific web server.

options.B: False

questions.question: Which techniques help manage 'State' in a horizontally scaled environment? (Select all that apply)

options.A: Using a distributed cache like Redis.
options.B: Storing state in a centralized SQL database.
options.C: Using JWT (JSON Web Tokens) to store state on the client side.
options.D: Saving state to the local hard drive of the web server.

questions.question: What is 'Database Federation'?

options.A: Merging all databases into a single global instance.
options.B: Splitting a monolithic database into multiple functional databases (e.g., User DB, Product DB).
options.C: A backup protocol for cloud databases.
options.D: Using only NoSQL databases.

questions.question: True or False: A 'Circuit Breaker' pattern is used to prevent a failing service from causing a cascading failure across the entire system.

options.B: False

questions.question: Which of these describe 'Blue-Green' deployment? (Select all that apply)

options.A: Two identical production environments running simultaneously.
options.B: Traffic is switched from the old version (Blue) to the new version (Green) via a load balancer.
options.C: Allows for near-instant rollback if the new version fails.
options.D: Requires users to re-install the application.

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of 'Read Replicas'?

options.A: To handle the write-heavy load of the application.
options.B: To scale read throughput by offloading SELECT queries from the primary database.
options.C: To act as the primary source of truth for transactions.
options.D: To encrypt the data at rest.

questions.question: True or False: 'Write-Through' caching ensures that data is written to the cache and the backend store simultaneously, providing high consistency.

options.B: False

questions.question: Which of these can result in 'Cache Invalidation' issues? (Select all that apply)

options.A: Stale data appearing to users because the cache wasn't updated after a database write.
options.B: Race conditions where two processes update the cache with different values.
options.C: The cache server running out of memory.
options.D: The database being too fast for the cache.

questions.question: What problem does 'Consistent Hashing' solve when scaling a distributed cache cluster?

options.A: It ensures all data is encrypted before storage.
options.B: It minimizes the number of keys that need to be remapped when a node is added or removed from the cluster.
options.C: It prevents the 'Thundering Herd' problem.
options.D: It synchronizes the system clock across all nodes.

questions.question: True or False: The PACELC theorem states that if there is a partition (P), one must choose between Availability (A) and Consistency (C); Else (E), when the system is running normally, one must choose between Latency (L) and Consistency (C).

options.B: False

questions.question: Which of the following are characteristics of 'Gossip Protocols' in distributed systems? (Select all that apply)

options.A: Information is spread across the cluster in an exponential manner.
options.B: It is highly resilient to node failures.
options.C: It is used for cluster membership and failure detection.
options.D: It requires a centralized master node to coordinate messages.

questions.question: In a distributed database, what is a 'Quorum' for a successful write operation?

options.A: All replicas must acknowledge the write.
options.B: A defined number of replicas (usually W + R > N) must acknowledge the operation to ensure consistency.
options.C: Only the master node needs to acknowledge the write.
options.D: The user must refresh their browser.

questions.question: True or False: 'Linearizability' is a stronger consistency guarantee than 'Eventual Consistency'.

options.B: False

questions.question: Which of the following describes 'Write Amplification' in distributed systems? (Select all that apply)

options.A: A single logical write resulting in multiple physical writes across different replicas.
options.B: Increased storage I/O due to background compaction or index updates.
options.C: The user sending the same request twice.
options.D: The database growing in size due to log-structured merge-trees.

questions.question: What is 'Backpressure' in a streaming or message-based architecture?

options.A: The physical air pressure inside a server chassis.
options.B: A mechanism where a downstream service signals to an upstream service to slow down because it is overwhelmed.
options.C: A way to speed up the database.
options.D: A security protocol for firewalls.

questions.question: True or False: 'Vector Clocks' are used to determine the partial ordering of events in a distributed system and detect causality violations.

options.B: False

questions.question: Which of these are challenges associated with 'Multi-Master' replication? (Select all that apply)

options.A: Conflict resolution when two masters update the same record simultaneously.
options.B: Increased write latency to ensure all masters are in sync.
options.C: Complexity in maintaining global unique identifiers (GUIDs).
options.D: It is impossible to use with SQL databases.
